content: Is man one of God's blunders? Or is God one of man's blunders?
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Friedrich Nietzsche understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
